items.name: Frozen Butterbeer
items.description: A butterscotch and shortbread-flavored slush topped with a thick sweet cream foam, sold non-alcoholic from carts along Hogsmeade street and inside the Three Broomsticks.
items.verdict: The single thing to eat or drink at Universal Orlando if you only do one. The frozen version beats the cold one comfortably in Florida heat and it is the reason the carts exist.

items.name: Butterbeer
items.description: The original chilled version of Butterbeer, a cream soda base with butterscotch and shortbread notes under a thick foam cap, served in a plastic cup or a souvenir tankard.
items.verdict: Closer to what the books describe and sweeter than most people expect. Worth ordering once to compare, and the frozen version is the one you will finish.

items.name: Hot Butterbeer
items.description: The warm version of Butterbeer, closer to a butterscotch steamer with the same cream foam floated on top, served from the Three Broomsticks and the Hog's Head.
items.verdict: The best of the three on a rare cold Florida morning and an odd choice on any other day. Order it in January, not July.

items.name: Butterbeer Soft-Serve
items.description: Butterbeer flavor as a soft-serve ice cream, sold in a cup or a cone from the Hogsmeade carts.
items.verdict: Better than the cold drink and worse than the frozen one. Good with two spoons and a child who has already had a Butterbeer and wants another.

items.name: Butterbeer Potted Cream
items.description: A small pot of butterscotch custard with a cream layer and a shortbread element, served as dessert at the Three Broomsticks.
items.verdict: The most interesting form Butterbeer takes and the one nobody orders. Get it if you are already eating here; it is not worth a special queue.

items.name: Rotisserie Smoked Chicken
items.description: Half a smoked rotisserie chicken with corn on the cob and roasted potatoes, served on a metal tray in the Three Broomsticks dining hall.
items.verdict: The best thing on the Hogsmeade menu and one of the two best quick-service plates in the park. Order this rather than the shepherd's pie and share it if you are not hungry.

items.name: Shepherd's Pie
items.description: Minced lamb and vegetables under a mashed potato crust, baked and served in its own dish with a side salad.
items.verdict: Competent and heavy, and a strange thing to eat in Florida in August. It works in winter and it is the wrong order at 90 degrees.

items.name: Fish and Chips
items.description: Beer-battered cod fillets with thick-cut chips, served with tartar sauce in the Three Broomsticks.
items.verdict: Genuinely decent batter and a large portion. Not a reason to queue, and a perfectly good thing to eat once you are inside.

items.name: Hog's Head Brew
items.description: A Scottish-style ale brewed specifically for the Hog's Head pub in Hogsmeade and not sold at Diagon Alley across the lagoon.
items.verdict: An actual good beer rather than a themed novelty, and exclusive to this pub. The right order for an adult who has had enough butterscotch.

items.name: Pumpkin Juice
items.description: A chilled spiced apple and pumpkin drink sold in a labeled bottle from the Magic Neep cart and the Hogsmeade counters.
items.verdict: Sweeter and more like spiced apple juice than the name suggests. Worth trying once, and the empty bottle is a better souvenir than the drink is a beverage.

items.name: Chocolate Frog
items.description: A large solid milk chocolate frog in an ornate pentagonal box, packaged with a collectible wizard card.
items.verdict: Overrated as chocolate and reasonable as a souvenir. You are paying seventeen dollars for a card and a box; buy it knowing that, and buy a cauldron cake if you want dessert.

items.name: Cauldron Cake
items.description: A dense chocolate cake shaped like a cauldron, filled with chocolate mousse and finished with a fondant handle.
items.verdict: The best thing in Honeydukes to actually eat, and a third the price of the Chocolate Frog. Rich enough that one is plenty between two people.

items.name: Pumpkin Pasty
items.description: A hand-sized pastry turnover filled with spiced pumpkin, sold from the counter at Honeydukes and from the Hogsmeade carts.
items.verdict: Closer to a pumpkin pie in a crust than anything savory, and better than it looks under the shop lights. A good portable option for eating in a queue.

items.name: Exploding Bon Bons
items.description: Chocolate truffles containing popping candy, sold in a decorated box from the Honeydukes counter.
items.verdict: Fifteen dollars for popping candy in a truffle. The packaging is doing all the work here, and the fudge counter is better value in the same shop.

items.name: Honeydukes Fudge
items.description: House-made fudge sold by the slice from a counter at the back of Honeydukes, in rotating flavors including chocolate, peanut butter and sea salt caramel.
items.verdict: The best-value sweet purchase in Honeydukes and the one almost nobody looks at. Ask for a sample first - the flavors vary more in quality than the display suggests.

items.name: Quarter Rotisserie Chicken
items.description: A quarter of a chicken cooked on a wood-fired rotisserie, served with rice and black beans and a piece of grilled corn.
items.verdict: The best quick-service plate at Universal Orlando and better than any counter-service main at Walt Disney World. It costs the same as a burger a hundred yards away. Order it.

items.name: Baby Back Ribs Platter
items.description: A half rack of wood-smoked baby back ribs with corn on the cob and rice and beans, served on a tray in the Thunder Falls dining room.
items.verdict: Genuinely good smoked ribs at a price no table-service restaurant would match. Slightly less consistent than the chicken, and still one of the two best things in the park.

items.name: Smoked Turkey Leg
items.description: A large smoked turkey leg, cured so that it tastes closer to ham than to roast turkey, sold to eat in the dining room or carry out.
items.verdict: The standard theme park turkey leg, done properly here because it comes off the same wood fire as the chicken. Enormous, salty and genuinely shareable between two.

items.name: Double Cheeseburger
items.description: A double-patty cheeseburger with fries, finished at a self-serve toppings bar with lettuce, tomato, onions, pickles and sauces.
items.verdict: Ordinary until you use the toppings bar, which is the only thing separating it from every other burger here. Thunder Falls Terrace is two minutes away and much better.

items.name: Personal Pepperoni Pizza
items.description: A single-serving pepperoni pizza from the outdoor window on the lagoon side of Jurassic Park, served with a side salad option.
items.verdict: Exactly what a theme park window pizza is, and no worse than that. It buys you a short queue and a shaded table, which is sometimes the whole point.

items.name: Frozen Margarita
items.description: A frozen lime margarita from the covered outdoor bar between the Jurassic Park visitor complex and the VelociCoaster entrance.
items.verdict: Sweet, cold and fine, and mainly an excuse to sit in the shade underneath the VelociCoaster launch. The seat is worth more than the drink.

items.name: Fresh Whole Fruit
items.description: Whole apples, bananas and oranges sold from the small stand near the Camp Jurassic entrance, alongside bottled drinks and packaged snacks.
items.verdict: Unglamorous and genuinely useful. This is the easiest place in a park full of fryers to buy a child something that is not fried, and it costs three dollars.

items.name: Green Eggs and Ham Tots
items.description: A bowl of tater tots loaded with diced ham, cheese sauce and a green herb sauce that supplies the color, served from the ham-shaped building in Seuss Landing.
items.verdict: The best novelty dish at Universal Orlando and one of very few gimmick foods worth ordering twice. The green is herbs, not dye, and the acidity is what makes it work. One bowl feeds two.

items.name: The Whoburger
items.description: The house cheeseburger at Green Eggs and Ham Cafe, served with fries from the same window as the tots.
items.verdict: Filler on a menu that exists for one dish. Order the tots and skip this unless somebody in your group will only eat a burger.

items.name: Moose Juice
items.description: A frozen tangerine slush sold from the Seuss Landing stand of the same name, in a bright orange cup.
items.verdict: The sweeter of the two and the one children actually finish. A good cold drink at a low price in the island where you most need one.

items.name: Goose Juice
items.description: A frozen sour green apple slush, the tart counterpart to Moose Juice, sold from the same Seuss Landing stand.
items.verdict: Sharper than children expect and frequently abandoned half-finished. Ask before letting a five-year-old choose by color.

items.name: Hot Fudge Sundae
items.restaurant: Hop On Pop Ice Cream Shop
items.description: Hard-scoop vanilla ice cream with hot fudge, whipped cream and a cherry, from the small window in Seuss Landing.
items.verdict: Standard ice cream with a queue a fraction the size of the ones in Hogsmeade. The correct bribe for a child who has just been measured and turned away.

items.name: Fried Chicken Platter
items.description: Fried chicken with a side and a roll, served in the big-top dining hall where the Seuss trolley train passes overhead.
items.verdict: Adequate counter fried chicken. You are eating here for the air conditioning, the space and the trolley overhead, and that is a fair trade with a tired four-year-old.

items.name: Braised Short Rib
items.description: Slow-braised beef short rib with a potato puree and a reduced braising jus, the long-standing signature main at Mythos.
items.verdict: The best plate of food inside Islands of Adventure and cheaper than the equivalent at any Walt Disney World signature. This is the dish that justifies booking a table at all.

items.name: Pad Thai
items.description: Rice noodles with tamarind, peanuts, egg and vegetables, available with chicken, shrimp or as a vegetarian plate, and a fixture on the Mythos menu for years.
items.verdict: An odd dish to find in a Greek-themed cave and one of the most reliably good things on the menu. The vegetarian version is the best meat-free main in the park.

items.name: Crab Cake Sandwich
items.description: A lump crab cake on a brioche bun with slaw and a remoulade, served with fries at lunch.
items.verdict: More crab than filler, which is not a given at this price point in a theme park. The lighter lunch order if the short rib is too much at midday.

items.name: Gyro
items.description: Seasoned gyro meat in pita with tzatziki, tomato and onion, served with fries from the small window in The Lost Continent.
items.verdict: Better than the price and the location suggest, with no queue sixty seconds from the worst queues in the park. The smartest cheap lunch at Islands of Adventure.

items.name: Chicken Skewer
items.description: A grilled marinated chicken skewer cooked to order at the outdoor kebab window in The Lost Continent.
items.verdict: One of the only hot meals in this park you can eat while walking, and naturally gluten-free. Not exciting, and exactly right when you do not want to lose an hour to lunch.

items.name: The Dagwood
items.description: A very tall stacked deli sandwich of layered meats, cheese and salad on rye, named for the character in the Blondie comic strip who gave the sandwich style its name.
items.verdict: Made to order rather than pulled from a warmer, which puts it ahead of most counters here. It feeds two people comfortably, and there is nowhere shaded to sit and eat it.

items.name: Fish and Chips
items.description: Battered fish and fries from the fish and chips station in the Comic Strip Cafe food court.
items.verdict: The most reliable of the four stations in a food court where none of them are good. The air-conditioned room is the reason to be here, not this.

items.name: Bacon Cheeseburger
items.description: A bacon cheeseburger with fries, eaten in a comic-styled dining room looking out across the lagoon toward Hogsmeade.
items.verdict: An unremarkable burger with the best quick-service view in the park. Order it for the window seat and eat properly in Jurassic Park instead.

items.name: Cheese Pizza Slice
items.description: A large slice of cheese pizza from the counter in the Baxter Building on Marvel Super Hero Island, sold individually or as part of a whole pie.
items.verdict: Ordinary and useful. Buying the whole pie for a group is meaningfully cheaper than four slices, and the upstairs room is the only air conditioning on that plaza.

items.name: Mediterranean Hummus Platter
items.description: Hummus with warm pita, olives, feta and vegetables, served as a starter or a shared plate at Confisco Grille and the Backwater Bar.
items.verdict: The best vegan-friendly plate in the park outside Mythos, and large enough to be a light lunch for two. Order it at the Backwater Bar and skip the reservation entirely.

items.name: Classic Cinnabon
items.description: The standard Cinnabon cinnamon roll with cream cheese frosting, from the franchise counter in Port of Entry.
items.verdict: Exactly the thing you already know, at a theme park markup. The four-pack of MiniBons is the better order if more than one person wants some.

items.name: Chocolate Croissant
items.description: A laminated chocolate croissant from the bakery case a short walk inside the turnstiles, sold alongside sandwiches and coffee.
items.verdict: A decent pastry at a fair price, and the sensible way to eat breakfast inside the gates. Buy it at 8:30 and eat it walking to Hogsmeade.

items.name: Croissant Breakfast Sandwich
items.description: Egg, cheese and meat on a croissant, made in the morning at the Port of Entry bakery and available until the pastries run out.
items.verdict: A real breakfast for less than a hotel counter charges, and portable enough to eat on the walk to the first ride. The best breakfast decision inside the park.
